correctness.rationale: The formula is true. Iterating the derivative of a constant A gives (AA*)^(2^(k-1)); the normalized trace makes the first two diagonal matrix units, scaled by N^(1/q), a copy of l_q^2. With b=epsilon/2 and a=(1-b^q)^(1/q), the pair (a,b),(a,-b) has unit norms, separation epsilon, and midpoint norm a, also at epsilon=2. The cited Corollary 4.2 gives the opposite bound, but the paper's global setup takes prime-power sizes. To justify the frozen all-N quantifier, choose a power of two M>=N and use the isometric corner map F -> (M/N)^(1/q)(F direct_sum 0). Each k-fold derivative scales by (M/N) and stays in the corner, which cancels the normalized-trace change. The lower bound thus descends to every N. This also supplies the missing explicit scope justification in the frozen citation. No numerical or formal proof certification was used.
residual_risks: The proof concerns the full function space; it does not transfer the extremizers to the quantum Weyl-orbit subspace.
